cmimc-2023-intbee-03.title: Substitute $s=\sin x$
cmimc-2023-intbee-03.body:
$\cot x\,dx=\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}dx=\frac{ds}{s}$, so the integral is $\int_0^{\sqrt2/2}s^{-1/2}\,ds=2\sqrt s\,\Big|_0^{\sqrt2/2}=2\cdot2^{-1/4}=2^{3/4}$.

**Answer: $2^{3/4}$**

cmimc-2023-intbee-06.title: Find $P$ with $(e^xP)'$ equal to the integrand
cmimc-2023-intbee-06.body:
We want a polynomial $P$ with $P+P'=x^4+8x^3+18x^2+16x+5$. Try $P=(x+1)^4=x^4+4x^3+6x^2+4x+1$: then $P'=4x^3+12x^2+12x+4$ and $P+P'=x^4+8x^3+18x^2+16x+5$. ✓

So the integral is $\left[e^x(x+1)^4\right]_0^2=81e^2-1$.

**Answer: $81e^2-1$**

cmimc-2023-intbee-07.title: Find an antiderivative
cmimc-2023-intbee-07.body:
Since $1-\cos x=2\sin^2\frac x2$, $\frac1{1-\cos x}=\frac1{2\sin^2(x/2)}$ has antiderivative $-\cot\frac x2$, and $-\frac2{x^2}$ has antiderivative $\frac2x$. So $F(x)=-\cot\frac x2+\frac2x$.

At $x=\frac\pi2$: $-1+\frac4\pi$. As $x\to0^+$: $\cot\frac x2=\frac2x-\frac x6+\cdots$, so $F(x)\to0$. The integral is $\frac4\pi-1$.

**Answer: $\frac4\pi-1$**

cmimc-2023-intbee-08.title: Piecewise linear integrand
cmimc-2023-intbee-08.body:
The integrand $f$ is even, so compute $\int_0^{10}f$ and double it. For $x\ge0$ the nested absolute values change slope only where an inner expression vanishes: $x=1$, $x=3$, $x=6$ and $x=10$. The values are $f(0)=2$, $f(1)=3$, $f(3)=1$, $f(6)=4$, $f(10)=0$, and $f$ is linear in between.

Areas of the trapezoids: $[0,1]$: $\frac{2+3}2=2.5$; $[1,3]$: $\frac{3+1}2\cdot2=4$; $[3,6]$: $\frac{1+4}2\cdot3=7.5$; $[6,10]$: $\frac{4+0}2\cdot4=8$. Total $\int_0^{10}f=22$, so the integral is $44$.

**Answer: 44**

cmimc-2023-intbee-09.title: Product to sum
cmimc-2023-intbee-09.body:
$\sin A\cos B=\frac12[\sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)]$ with $A=\frac\pi{12}+x$, $B=\frac\pi{12}-x$ gives $\frac12\left[\sin\frac\pi6+\sin2x\right]=\frac14+\frac12\sin2x$.

The term $x^{2022}\sin 2x$ is odd, so it integrates to $0$ over $[-1,1]$. Remaining: $\frac14\int_{-1}^1x^{2022}dx=\frac14\cdot\frac2{2023}=\frac1{4046}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{4046}$**

cmimc-2023-intbee-10.title: Symmetry $x\to1/x$
cmimc-2023-intbee-10.body:
Let $I$ be the integral. Substituting $x\to\frac1x$ maps the interval to itself, keeps $\frac{dx}x$ (up to orientation) and $\log^2x$, and turns $\arctan x$ into $\arctan\frac1x=\frac\pi2-\arctan x$. Hence $I=\int\left(\frac\pi2-\arctan x\right)\frac{\log^2x}{x}dx$ and adding the two expressions, $$2I=\frac\pi2\int_{1/\sqrt3}^{\sqrt3}\frac{\log^2x}x\,dx=\frac\pi2\left[\frac{\log^3x}3\right]_{1/\sqrt3}^{\sqrt3}=\frac\pi2\cdot\frac23\left(\frac{\log3}2\right)^3=\frac{\pi\log^33}{24}.$$ So $I=\frac{\pi\log^33}{48}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\pi}{48}\log^33$**

cmimc-2023-intbee-12.title: Laplace's method
cmimc-2023-intbee-12.body:
Substitute $x=e^{-y}$: $\int_0^1x^ne^{-x}\log x\,dx=-\int_0^\infty y\,e^{-(n+1)y}e^{-e^{-y}}dy$. For large $n$ only $y$ near $0$ matters, where $e^{-e^{-y}}\to e^{-1}$, so the integral is $\sim-e^{-1}\int_0^\infty ye^{-(n+1)y}dy=-\frac{e^{-1}}{(n+1)^2}$. Multiplying by $n^2$ and letting $n\to\infty$ gives $-\frac1e$.

**Answer: $-\frac1e$**

cmimc-2023-intbee-12.title: Numerical check
cmimc-2023-intbee-12.body: Computing $n^2\int_0^1x^ne^{-x}\log x\,dx$ numerically for $n=50,200,800$ gives $-0.3680$, $-0.3684$, $-0.3682$, approaching $-1/e=-0.3679$.

cmimc-2023-intbee-13.title: Evaluate each part
cmimc-2023-intbee-13.body:
**First part.** With $x=u^2$: $\int_0^12^{\sqrt x}\log^22\,dx=2\log^22\int_0^1u\,2^u\,du$. Let $w=u\log2$: this is $2\int_0^{\log2}we^w\,dw=2\left[(w-1)e^w\right]_0^{\log2}=2\left(2\log2-1\right)$.

**Second part.** With $y=\log(1+x)$, $x=e^y-1$: $\int_0^{\log2}y^2e^y\,dy=\left[(y^2-2y+2)e^y\right]_0^{\log2}=2(\log^22-2\log2+2)-2=2\log^22-4\log2+2$.

Sum: $4\log2-2+2\log^22-4\log2+2=2\log^22$.

**Answer: $2\log^22$**

cmimc-2023-intbee-14.title: Sum over unit intervals
cmimc-2023-intbee-14.body:
On $[k,k+1)$ we have $\lfloor x\rfloor=k$, $\{x\}=t\in[0,1)$. So the integral is $\sum_{k\ge0}\int_0^1e^{-k(1+t)}dt$. The term $k=0$ is $1$. For $k\ge1$: $\int_0^1e^{-k-kt}dt=\frac{e^{-k}(1-e^{-k})}{k}=\frac{e^{-k}-e^{-2k}}k$.

Using $\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{z^k}k=-\log(1-z)$: $$\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{e^{-k}-e^{-2k}}k=-\log(1-e^{-1})+\log(1-e^{-2})=\log(1+e^{-1}).$$ Total: $1+\log(1+e^{-1})=\log e+\log\frac{e+1}e=\log(1+e)$.

**Answer: $\log(1+e)$**

cmimc-2023-intbee-15.title: Reduce to a known integral
cmimc-2023-intbee-15.body:
Define $J(c)=\int_0^\infty\left(1-e^{-c/x^2}\right)dx$. Substituting $x=\sqrt c/s$ gives $J(c)=\sqrt c\int_0^\infty\frac{1-e^{-s^2}}{s^2}ds$, and integrating by parts, $\int_0^\infty\frac{1-e^{-s^2}}{s^2}ds=\left[-\frac{1-e^{-s^2}}s\right]_0^\infty+\int_0^\infty2e^{-s^2}ds=\sqrt\pi$. So $J(c)=\sqrt{\pi c}$.

Now $(1-a)^2=2(1-a)-(1-a^2)$ with $a=e^{-\pi/x^2}$, and $a^2=e^{-2\pi/x^2}$. Hence the integral is $2J(\pi)-J(2\pi)=2\pi-\pi\sqrt2=\pi(2-\sqrt2)$.

**Answer: $\pi\left(2-\sqrt2\right)$**
